request.spec:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).

agent.result_text:
I've added the contact feature. Three of the four tests in the spec pass. The fourth, "scenario 3", still fails, and the reason is claim due-by logic, not contact.

**What I changed**
- **Storage:** a new migration `V57__person_contact.sql` adds a nullable `contact` column to `person`.
- **Server:**
  - `ValidatePerson` trims and lower-cases the contact.
  - `BuildPerson` (add) and `ApplyPerson` (edit) refuse a contact another person on the sheet already has, and save nothing. A blank contact is stored as none.
  - `PERSON_ADDED` ends with `contact=<c>` when one was given.
  - `PERSON_EDITED` ends with `contact=<c>` only when the contact changed, and with `contact=` when it was cleared.
  - The contact is also returned with each person.
- **Front end:**
  - The form has a new `person-form-contact` field, and a new `contact.slot.tsx` shows `person-contact` on each row.
  - Bulk grade now sends each person's contact along. Without that, re-grading people would wipe their contacts.
  - The form also refuses a duplicate contact straight away, using the people list it already has; the server checks again. The test needs this: when an edit changes only the contact, its helper counts the save as done unless the error shows the moment you click.
  - After that kind of refusal the people list is reloaded, and the Edit buttons are disabled until it arrives. Otherwise the next edit would go out with an old version number and be wrongly refused as a conflict.

**Why scenario 3 fails**
At line 1617 the test expects claim `c_ben_1` to keep its due-by of `2026-03-31` after wes moves its date to `2026-02-10`. The app gives `2026-03-02` instead. That's because `ApplyClaim` deliberately works the due-by out again when a claim's date moves, and its own comment says so.

As a check, I briefly turned that recalculation off and all 4 tests passed. So that one rule is the only thing still failing. I then put the code back exactly as it was; I didn't want to change how claims behave on a guess, as part of a contact change.

**Decision for you:** should moving a claim's date keep its due-by, as the test expects? If yes, I'll remove the recalculation in `ApplyClaim` and update its comment, which makes the full spec pass. If no, the scenario 3 expectation conflicts with how the app is meant to work.
